approved.description:
⛔ NOT marked required, and that is the handler's behaviour rather than a
gap: nothing rejects an absent `approved`, so `{}` is a valid body and
Go's zero value makes it a REJECTION. A generated SDK will let a caller
omit the one field that decides the outcome. Reported, not fixed —
making it required here would change what the endpoint accepts.

max_value.description:
⚠️ Called "required for evm_value_limit" but the handler does not enforce
that: it only validates the format when the field is non-empty. A
conditional requirement a flat `required` list cannot express anyway.

approved.description:
⛔ NOT required — same trap as the single-request endpoint: absent means
false, which REJECTS every id in the batch. Reported, not fixed.

request_ids.description:
Rejected when absent, empty, or entirely blank after trimming: 400
"request_ids is required and must not be empty".

sign_type.description:
⛔ Must be the literal "transaction"; anything else is 400 even though it
is a valid sign_type on the single-sign endpoint.

transaction.description:
Rejected when zero-length. ⚠️ Generated as `{"type":"object"}` via the
.swaggo json.RawMessage override; the real shape is an EVM transaction
object.

requests.description:
Rejected when absent or empty: 400 "requests array is required and must
not be empty". Capped at 20 items.

transactions.description: Rejected when absent or empty (400), capped at 20.

chain_id.description: Rejected when empty or not a positive decimal integer — one combined 400.

signed_tx_hex.description: Rejected when empty or not 0x-prefixed hex — one combined 400.

signer_address.description:
SignerAddress is set for kind=simulation budgets, decoded from the
"sim:<address>" rule_id used by the simulation fallback. Real-rule
budgets keep this empty (the signer is implicit from the rule's
own scope).

alert_pct.description: Not required: 0 is replaced by the default 80.

max_per_tx.description: Not required: empty means unlimited and becomes "-1".

max_total.description:
MaxTotal is required, and the reason is not the field name: the check is
isValidBudgetLimit, which rejects the empty string, so an absent
max_total is 400 "max_total must be a non-negative decimal or \"-1\"".
⚠️ Contrast MaxPerTx below, whose check is guarded by `!= ""`.

max_tx_count.description: Not required: 0 is a meaningful value (no tx-count cap) and passes.

rule_id.description: RuleID is rejected when blank after trimming: 400 "rule_id is required".

unit.description: Unit is rejected when blank after trimming: 400 "unit is required".

action.description:
⚠️ Action is NOT required even though it looks like the discriminator:
createOrImport's switch reads `case "create", "":`, so an absent action
means create. Only an unrecognised value is a 400.

entropy_bits.description: For create. Not required: 0 means "let the manager choose".

mnemonic.description:
For import — exactly one of Mnemonic / WalletJSON should be set.

⛔ Neither is marked required and neither could be: they are required
only when action is "import" (400 "mnemonic or wallet_json is required
for import"), and then exactly one of the two (400 "specify either
mnemonic or wallet_json, not both"). That is a conditional exactly-one-of,
which a flat `required` list cannot say — marking either one would reject
every create request in a generated SDK.

password.description:
Password is rejected when empty: 400 "password is required", checked
before the action switch so it applies to create AND import.

Required WHENEVER this object is present, which is exactly what a schema
`required` means: Validate answers ErrEmptyPassword → 400. There is no
path on which a present keystore object with an empty password succeeds.

private_key_hex.description:
⛔ At most one of these two, and neither is required — leaving both empty
creates a fresh keypair. Sending both is 400 "specify private_key_hex or
keystore_json, not both". An at-most-one-of, which no required list says.

applied_to.description:
⚠️ Only admin may set this to anything but the default; a non-admin
naming other keys is a 400 from the ownership resolver.

config.description:
⚠️ NOT marked required even though it has no omitempty and most rule
types need it: the emptiness check lives in ValidateRuleConfig, which is
per rule TYPE, so whether an absent config is a 400 depends on `type`.
A flat required list cannot say that.

mode.description:
Rejected when empty: 400 "mode is required"; then must be exactly
"whitelist" or "blocklist".

name.description: Rejected when empty: 400 "name is required" (rule_crud.go createRule).

test_cases.description:
⚠️ "required for evm_js" is a per-type rule enforced during validation,
not a field-level required. Left optional for the same reason as Config.

keystore.description:
⚠️ NOT marked required although a keystore-type create cannot succeed
without it (ErrMissingKeystoreParams → 400): the requirement is
conditional on `type`, which a flat required list cannot express.

type.description:
Rejected when empty: types.CreateSignerRequest.Validate answers
ErrMissingSignerType for the empty case, which the handler turns into 400.

variables.description:
See the note on config.TestCaseConfig.Variables: every mirror of the
test-case shape must carry this, or per-case overrides vanish silently.

max_value.description:
⚠️ Not enforced as required for any rule type; only format-checked when
non-empty.

rule_mode.description:
Rejected when empty: 400 "rule_mode is required". ⚠️ Contrast the approval
endpoint, where rule_mode is optional.

approval_source.description:
ApprovalSource is one of "manual", "rule", "simulation" once the
request has been approved. Emitted even when the row predates the
column so the UI can render a single consistent "approved by …"
line for all three paths.

generatable_rule_types.description:
GeneratableRuleTypes lists rule types whose config can be auto-derived
from this request's payload. Only populated on GET detail while the
request is pending/authorizing — drives the approval panel dropdown.

last_no_match_reason.description:
LastNoMatchReason is the engine's diagnostic when no whitelist rule
matched; empty when a rule auto-approved. The popup activity
drawer renders this so operators see "why didn't my rule fire?"
without grepping server logs.

rule_generation_hints.description:
RuleGenerationHints carries optional defaults for generatable types
(e.g. max_value for evm_value_limit from the transaction value).

transaction_id.description:
TransactionID is the FK into /api/v1/evm/transactions; set
when the wallet RPC proxy observes a broadcast whose signed
bytes match this request's signed_data. The web UI renders
it as a status badge + link on the Requests list.

budget_period.description: e.g. "24h0m0s"; set when schedule.period is configured

chain_id.description:
Rejected when empty (400 "chain_id is required"), then parsed as a
positive decimal integer.

payload.description:
Rejected when zero-length (400 "payload is required"), capped at 2 MB.

⛔ The generated schema for this field is `{"type":"object"}` and that is
WRONG for some sign types — the real shape depends on sign_type, and for
`hash` / `raw_message` the payload is not an object. It renders that way
because .swaggo has to map json.RawMessage to interface{} for swag to
generate at all. Recorded there; do not read the schema as the payload
contract.

sign_type.description:
Rejected when empty (400 "sign_type is required"), then checked against
the known set.

signer_address.description:
Rejected when empty (400 "signer_address is required"), then checked as
0x + 40 hex.

locked.description:
Mirror types.SignerInfo's full surface so the web UI's HD wallet
detail panel can render derivation index, lock state, and the
parent-address backreference. Earlier versions dropped these
fields here on the way out, so listDerived's JSON looked like
{address, type, enabled} only — the UI fell back to "—" for
every index column.

primary_address.description: for HD derived: parent HD address; otherwise self

data.description: Optional, but checked as 0x-prefixed hex when non-empty.

gas.description: Optional; empty lets the simulator choose a gas limit.

to.description:
⛔ Required here, unlike a real transaction: this endpoint cannot
simulate a contract deployment (empty `to`).

value.description: Optional. Empty is passed through to the simulator as-is.

data.description: Optional, but checked as 0x-prefixed hex when non-empty.

to.description:
Rejected when empty or not an EVM address: 400
"transactions[i].to must be a valid 0x-prefixed Ethereum address".

password.description:
Rejected when empty: 400 "password is required" (signer_locking.go
handleUnlock, after the ownership check).

test_cases.description: required for evm_js when updating config

created_at.description:
⚠️ The four timestamps carry `format:"date-time"` for swag only. Without
it a time.Time generates as a bare `string` and a generated SDK hands the
caller an unparsed one; encoding/json really does write RFC 3339 here, so
the format is the truth and its absence was the lie.
⛔ It does not fix the other half: `last_used_at` and `expires_at` are
pointers and generate as non-nullable strings anyway — swag has no tag for
OpenAPI 3.1 nullability, so "absent" is the only signal a client gets.

signer_address.description:
SignerAddress is rejected when blank or absent: addMember returns 400
"signer_address is required".

skip_validation.description:
Parsed only to reject — never honored. See validation_mandatory.go.
⛔ Not required, and sending `true` is a 400 by design.

variables.description:
Variables is NOT required: a nil map is replaced by an empty one and the
preset's own defaults apply. ⚠️ What IS required cannot be said in a
schema — the preset's operator_overrides decide, per preset, which keys
must be present and non-empty, and a missing one is 400 "required
override %q not supplied". Call GET /api/v1/presets/{id} and read
`variables[].required` to learn which.

id.description:
ID is rejected when empty: createAPIKey returns 400 "id is required"
(apikey.go:297). Also capped at 64 chars and restricted to [a-zA-Z0-9-].

name.description: Name is rejected when empty: 400 "name is required" (apikey.go:311).

public_key.description:
PublicKey is rejected when empty: 400 "public_key is required"
(apikey.go:321). Ed25519 public key, hex or base64 DER.

rate_limit.description:
RateLimit is NOT required: 0 (the absent value) is replaced by the
default 100 at apikey.go:332, so omitting it is a supported call.

role.description:
Role is rejected when empty: 400 "role is required" (apikey.go:341).
One of admin, dev, agent, strategy.

budget_metering.description:
BudgetMetering (optional) configures how a template instance measures "spend amount"
for budget enforcement.

Expected keys:
- method: "none" | "count_only" | "tx_value" | "calldata_param" | "typed_data_field" | "js"
- unit:   budget identity string (recommended: include chain+asset identity, e.g. "${chain_id}:${token_address}")

Notes:
- For method "js" (evm_js rules), the script may implement validateBudget(input) and return bigint/decimal-string.

config.description:
⚠️ Config is NOT required despite having no omitempty: the handler
json.Marshals it with no emptiness check, so an absent config stores
`null` and creates the template. Reported rather than enforced — adding
the check would be a validation change.

mode.description: Mode is rejected when empty: 400 "mode is required".

name.description:
Name is rejected when empty: createTemplate returns 400 "name is
required" (template_handler.go, right after the decode).

type.description:
Type is rejected when empty: 400 "type is required". Must be a known
rule type or the meta type "template_bundle".

description.description:
Description has no check at all and its zero value is meaningful (a
wallet with no description), so it is optional.

name.description:
Name is rejected when blank or absent: createWallet returns 400
"name is required" (see the TrimSpace check below the decode).

skip_validation.description: Parsed only to reject — never honored. See validation_mandatory.go.

chain_type.description:
ChainType surfaces the template's chain family — empty for off-chain
templates (sign_type_allowlist etc.). The UI uses this for the
"Chain" column and for filtering; before R10 the column showed
every row as off-chain because this field was missing from the wire.

default.description:
Default is `any` server-side; the SDK types it as `unknown` and
stringifies in the UI when needed. Round-trip via json.RawMessage
preserves the natural shape (string / number / bool / array).

password.description:
Password is rejected when absent or empty: ServeAdmin returns 400
"password is required" (bootstrap.go, the `req.Password == ""` check).
See wallet.go for why `binding:"required"` is documentation-only here.

balance_changes.description:
BalanceChanges + Events + Contracts + DecodedCalldata are stored
as JSON so we don't have to maintain a separate schema per
field shape. The reading side decodes into typed structures
at the handler boundary.

decision.description:
Decision is what the simulation engine would tell the sign
service if the request were freshly evaluated right now.
Values: "allow", "deny", "no_match" (simulation skipped this
kind of request — e.g. a sign_type that isn't `transaction`),
"manual" (a managed-signer approve / dangerous state change
was detected — defer to operator).

decoded_calldata.description:
DecodedCalldata is the parsed (function name + args) view of
the transaction's calldata. Empty for sign_types that don't
carry calldata (personal_sign, typed_data).

raw_result.description:
RawResult is the unmodified SimulationResult JSON — kept as
a debug fallback so we can re-render or analyse a past
snapshot even after the decoded columns above shift shape.

reason.description:
Reason carries the human-readable explanation when Decision
is not "allow" (budget exceeded message, revert reason,
approval-detected note, etc.). Empty otherwise.

success.description:
Result snapshot (success / gas / revert reason). Mirrors the
SimulationResult shape so the SDK + UI can render without
having to crack open the RawResult blob.

applied_to.description:
AppliedTo controls which API keys this rule affects at runtime.
["*"] = all keys (admin only), ["self"] = owner only (default for non-admin),
["key-1", "key-2"] = specific keys (admin only).

approved_by.description: ApprovedBy: admin key ID that approved a pending rule.

budget_period.description:
Schedule fields — for periodic budget renewal
When BudgetPeriod is set, the instance automatically renews its budget
at each period boundary. ExpiresAt still controls the overall lifetime.

budget_period_start.description: when the first period begins (SQLite: datetime, PostgreSQL: timestamptz)

immutable.description: Immutable: when true, rule cannot be modified or deleted via API.

matrix.description:
Matrix is an optional per-chain variable override table.
When non-nil, the evaluator resolves variables for a request by first
loading Variables (defaults), then looking up Matrix[chain_id] and
merging the per-chain overrides on top. ChainID on the rule is nil
when Matrix is used — the rule matches ALL chains, but variables are
resolved per-request based on the sign-request's chain_id.
Stored as JSONB: []map[string]interface{}.

owner.description:
Ownership & scoping
Owner is the API key ID that created this rule. "config" for rules from config file / preset CLI.

proposal_for.description:
ProposalFor is set when this rule is a proposed update to another rule.
It points to the target rule ID. nil means this is a regular rule, not a proposal.
When the proposal is approved, the changes are applied to the target rule and
this proposal row is marked rejected (preserving the audit trail).

rejection_reason.description: RejectionReason stores why an admin rejected a pending_approval rule or proposal.

x-enum-comments.RuleTypeEVMAddressList: address list (whitelist mode = allow, blocklist mode = block)
x-enum-comments.RuleTypeEVMDynamicBlocklist: Dynamic blocklist: runtime-synced from external URLs (OFAC, scam DBs)
x-enum-comments.RuleTypeEVMJS: JS rules (in-process Sobek); validate(input) → { valid, reason?, payload? }
x-enum-comments.RuleTypeMessagePattern: regex pattern matching for personal sign messages

block_number.description: Mined details — nullable until the poller observes the receipt.

error_message.description:
ErrorMessage carries the upstream RPC reason for Failed status
(Broadcast rejection: "nonce too low", "intrinsic gas too low",
"underpriced"). Empty for non-failed states.

from_address.description:
FromAddress is the recovered signer (denormalised so the UI
doesn't have to join sign_requests to know who broadcast).

last_checked_at.description:
LastCheckedAt is updated every time the poller fetches a
receipt; lets us throttle per-tx polling without re-scanning
the whole pending set on every tick.

receipt_status.description:
ReceiptStatus: 0 = on-chain revert, 1 = success. Nil while not
yet mined; nil after dropped/failed.

sign_request_id.description:
SignRequestID is the originating sign request, if known. Empty
when the proxy can't match the broadcast to one we signed
(third-party caller hit the proxy with a pre-signed payload).

tx_hash.description:
TxHash is the keccak256 hash of the signed RLP — the canonical
identifier on chain. Indexed for poller lookups.

Ed25519Signature.description: ⚠️ An approximation: four headers are required, not one. X-API-Key-ID names the key; X-Timestamp, X-Nonce and X-Signature carry an Ed25519 signature over the canonical request (internal/api/middleware/auth.go). A client that sends only X-API-Key-ID is rejected with 401.
Ed25519Signature.name: X-API-Key-ID

info.description:
Policy-driven signing daemon: the API a client uses to ask for a signature and an operator uses to decide what may be signed.

⚠️ Authentication is an Ed25519 signature over the request, not a bearer token — see the Ed25519Signature scheme below for what the headers actually carry. OpenAPI has no vocabulary for "signature over method + path + body + timestamp", so a generated client CANNOT authenticate on the strength of this document alone; the signing step stays in the hand-written transport (pkg/client/transport).
info.title: Remote Signer API

get.description:
Read-only view of the IP allow-list the daemon booted with. Configured in config.yaml, not through this API — there is no write counterpart.
⚠️ When no whitelist is wired the handler answers 200 with `enabled:false` and both address lists null, not 404. "Disabled" and "not configured" are the same answer here.
Returns the group as the daemon is currently running it — the live snapshot, not what config.yaml said at boot.

put.description:
⛔ This REPLACES the whole group, it does not merge. The handler decodes the body into a zero-valued snapshot and persists that struct as it stands, so **every field absent from the body is written as its zero value** — omitting a field turns it off rather than leaving it alone. Read the group first and send it back with your edit applied.
⚠️ The 200 body is the manager's snapshot re-read after the write, so it can differ from what was sent if the store normalised anything.
⚠️ Error bodies here are a bare text/plain line, NOT the `{"error":...}` JSON every other endpoint answers with — the handler uses http.Error. ⛔ The 400 and 500 below still say `application/json` because swag's @Produce is per-operation and cannot vary by response; the schema is `string` and this sentence is the correction. Documented rather than fixed: making the handler answer JSON is a response-shape change.

put.description:
⭐ MERGE semantics, since 2026-09-16: a field **absent from the body keeps its current value**, and only fields actually present are written. To flip one switch, send that one field.
⛔ This differs from the other eight settings groups, which still REPLACE wholesale — see each of their descriptions. Security was changed first because half its fields are security switches and every omission failed in the same direction, **looser**: nonce_required / manual_approval_enabled / require_approval_for_agent_rules all default to true and became false; max_keystores_per_key / max_hd_wallets_per_key default to 5 / 3 and became 0 — and 0 on those two means **no limit**.
⚠️ Values you do write still apply, including `false` and `0`. Absence (JSON null / omitted key) is the only thing that means "leave it alone" — so a switch stays switchable off.
⚠️ The 200 body is the manager's snapshot re-read after the write, so it can differ from what was sent if the store normalised anything.
⚠️ Error bodies here are a bare text/plain line, NOT the `{"error":...}` JSON every other endpoint answers with — the handler uses http.Error. ⛔ The 400 and 500 below still say `application/json` because swag's @Produce is per-operation and cannot vary by response; the schema is `string` and this sentence is the correction. Documented rather than fixed: making the handler answer JSON is a response-shape change.

get.description:
⛔ The Ed25519 public key is never returned by any endpoint in this group — `toAPIKeyResponse` omits it deliberately.
⚠️ `limit` above 100 is clamped to 100 rather than rejected; a negative or non-numeric one is a 400.

parameters.description: restrict to keys from this source (config or api)
parameters.name: source

parameters.description: ⚠️ only `true` filters — `false` is parsed, then ignored, so it returns enabled and disabled alike
parameters.name: enabled

post.description:
⚠️ The caller supplies the public key; the daemon never generates or stores a private key for an API key, and nothing secret comes back in the response.
⚠️ New keys are always created enabled, with source `api`. Neither is settable.

403.description: api_keys_api_readonly is on in the security settings

get.description:
Authenticated but NOT permissioned: any valid key may call it, which is why the projection is deliberately narrower than the admin listing — id, name, role, enabled and nothing else.
⚠️ Enabled keys only, hard-capped at 500, with no paging parameters. A deployment past 500 keys silently sees a prefix.

delete.description:
⛔ Three lockout guards answer 400: you cannot delete your own key, you cannot delete the last enabled admin key, and a key that still owns signers must have them deleted or transferred first.
⚠️ On success the daemon cascades rules, applied_to and signer_access for the deleted key. A cascade failure is logged and does NOT change the 204 — the key is already gone by then.

400.description: own key, last admin key, or the key still owns signers

403.description: read-only mode, or the key came from config.yaml

put.description:
Partial: every field is a pointer and an absent one is left alone. `{}` is a valid body and a no-op.
⛔ Two self-protection rules answer 400, not 403: you cannot change your own role, and a config-sourced key cannot be modified through the API at all (that one is 403).

400.description: bad body, own role, empty/too-long name, unknown role, or rate_limit outside 1..10000

403.description: read-only mode, or the key came from config.yaml

get.description:
Cursor-paginated. Follow `next_cursor` **and** `next_cursor_id` together — the cursor is a RFC3339Nano timestamp and ties are broken by id, so sending one without the other skips or repeats rows.
⚠️ Filter validation is asymmetric and that is the handler's actual behaviour, not an oversight in this description: `event_type`, `severity`, `signer_address`, `chain_type`, `chain_id`, `exclude_event_type`, `start_time`, `end_time` and `cursor` answer 400 when malformed, while `limit` is silently ignored unless it is in 1..100 (the default 30 stands), and `api_key_id`, `sign_request_id` and `cursor_id` are taken as given with no validation at all.
⚠️ `total` is counted with the cursor filters removed, so it is the size of the whole filtered set rather than of the page.

parameters.name: api_key_id

parameters.name: sign_request_id

parameters.description: 1..100; anything else leaves the default 30 in place
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: audit id from next_cursor_id; pair it with cursor
parameters.name: cursor_id

post.description:
Unauthenticated by design and succeeds exactly once; two concurrent calls race fairly inside the creator and the loser gets 410.
⚠️ The 200 body carries ONE FIELD MORE than the schema below says: a constant `"status": "ok"` sits alongside the four AdminResult fields, which Go embedding flattens to the top level rather than nesting under a key. `keystore_json` is present only when the daemon returns the keystore inline.
⛔ The schema under-describes on purpose. The handler answers with an anonymous struct, which swag cannot name, and its `AdminResult{status=string}` composition syntax is worse than useless on v2.0.0-rc6 — measured: it emits a bogus top-level component literally named `status` AND rewrites the shared `bootstrap.AdminResult` component to claim a `status` field it does not have. Under-describing one response beats corrupting a shared schema; the honest fix is a named response type, which is a code change and not this step's job.
⛔ The password is never echoed back and the handler zeroises its copy before responding.

200.description: plus a constant `status: \"ok\"` field — see the description

410.description: the bootstrap window has closed; code=admin_already_exists

get.description:
Unauthenticated by design: the api_keys table is empty on first run, so there is no public key to verify a signed request against.
⚠️ "Needs bootstrap" means specifically "no api key with id=admin yet" — not "no keys at all". The agent key is provisioned at every first start, so a count-based check would flip to false and hide the bootstrap form.

post.description:
⛔ This endpoint does NOT sign and does NOT consult the rule engine: it forwards bytes the caller already holds to the chain's RPC. A transaction signed elsewhere goes out unexamined.
⚠️ An RPC rejection is 502, not 400 — including a rejection caused by the caller's own transaction (bad nonce, underpriced). The upstream message is passed through verbatim in `error`.

get.description:
⚠️ No query parameters and no paging: every budget row the caller may see comes back, and `total` is the length of that filtered list rather than a database count.
⚠️ Visibility is per row and a row the caller may not see is dropped silently.
⚠️ Rows whose budget period has rolled over are renewed on read, so a GET here is not side-effect free.
⚠️ `kind` separates real rule budgets from synthetic `simulation` ones, whose rule_id is `sim:<address>`.

post.description:
The budget id is derived from rule_id + unit, so the pair is the row's identity and cannot be changed later — an identity change is delete plus create.
⛔ A rule_id starting with `sim:` is 403: that namespace belongs to the simulation fallback and is not client-writable.
⚠️ Creating a budget for a rule that does not exist is 404, and a duplicate rule+unit is 409 rather than an idempotent 200.

403.description: rule_id is in the reserved sim: namespace

409.description: a budget already exists for this rule+unit

get.description: ⚠️ Narrowed per row by an access check, and a row whose access check ERRORS is skipped silently — an infrastructure failure looks like \"you do not have that wallet\" rather than a 500.

501.description: this build has no HD wallet manager

post.description:
⛔ Admin ROLE required, checked in the handler as 403. The route itself carries no permission at all, so this check is the only thing standing between an authenticated non-admin key and wallet creation.
⚠️ One endpoint, two operations: `action` selects them and an absent action means create. The import form additionally needs exactly one of `mnemonic` / `wallet_json`.
⛔ The password, mnemonic and wallet JSON are zeroised in memory after use and none of them is ever echoed back.
⚠️ Ownership of the new wallet is recorded as active for an admin and pending-approval otherwise — and a FAILURE to record it is logged, not surfaced: the 201 still says the wallet was created.

403.description: not admin, read-only mode, or the per-key HD wallet limit is reached

501.description: this build has no HD wallet manager

Two forms: `{\"index\": n}` derives one, `{\"start\": n, \"count\": m}` derives a range of 1..100. An empty body is a 400.
⚠️ A locked wallet answers 423, not 403 — unlock it rather than re-authenticating.
⚠️ A wallet this key may not touch is 403, not 404; an `address` that is not a well-formed EVM address is 400.

parameters.description: primary address of the HD wallet, 0x + 40 hex
parameters.name: address

⚠️ `limit` outside 1..100 is silently ignored (the default 20 stands), while every other malformed filter is a 400.
⚠️ Always narrowed to EVM regardless of what is asked.

post.description:
⛔ `approved` defaults to FALSE, so a body carrying only `request_ids` REJECTS all of them.
⚠️ Partial success is normal and arrives as 200: per-id outcomes are in `results[].error` and the counts in `summary`. A 4xx here means the batch was refused before any of it ran.
⚠️ Blank ids are dropped silently rather than rejected; a list of only blanks is a 400.
⛔ A caller without approve_request permission must own the signer behind EVERY id — one foreign id fails the whole call with 403 before anything is decided.
⚠️ `idempotent: true` on a row means that request had already been decided and this call did not change it.

403.description: not the owner of every signer in the batch

post.summary: Approve or reject several sign requests

get.description:
⚠️ Carries the decoded payload and, when the request is still pending, rule-generation hints the approval endpoint can act on.
⚠️ This route carries no permission on purpose: who may read a row is a per-row decision the handler makes, and a request belonging to another key answers 403.

403.description: the request belongs to another api key

post.description:
⛔ `approved` decides everything and defaults to FALSE. An empty body `{}` REJECTS the request — there is no \"you forgot to say\" error.
⚠️ Supplying `rule_type` additionally generates a rule from this request so the next identical one is decided automatically; the new rule comes back in `generated_rule`. Omitting it approves this request only.
⚠️ A locked signer answers 423, and a request already decided answers 409.
⛔ Authorization is per row: a key without approve_request permission may still approve, but only for a signer it owns.

requestBody.description: the decision, and optionally a rule to generate

403.description: not the signer owner, or rule generation while security.rules_api_readonly is on

post.summary: Approve or reject a sign request

post.description:
Read-only dry run: returns the rule that POST .../approve WOULD create for this request, without creating it and without deciding the request.
⚠️ Stricter than the approval endpoint it previews: `rule_mode` is required here and optional there.
⚠️ Every generator failure is a 400 with a rewritten operator-facing message.

200.description: the rule that would be created; nothing is persisted

403.description: the request belongs to another api key

post.summary: Preview the rule an approval would generate

get.description:
⛔ 404 has TWO meanings here and the message is the only way to tell them apart: \"request not found\" (no such id, or it belongs to someone else) and \"simulation not yet available\" (the request exists and the pipeline has not finished). The UI polls on the second.
⛔ A request owned by another api key is 404, never 403 — telling them apart would let any key enumerate request ids.

404.description: no such request, not yours, or the simulation is not ready yet

get.description:
⛔ Scoped and REDACTED per caller: admin and dev see every rule, an agent or strategy key sees only rules that apply to it, and an AGENT key gets `config` stripped to null so rule script source never reaches it. `total` is recomputed after that filtering.
⚠️ `enabled`, `limit` and `offset` are parsed leniently — a malformed value leaves the default; the other filters answer 400.

post.description:
⛔ TWO success codes, and the difference matters: 201 means the rule is ACTIVE and already deciding sign requests; 202 means it was stored as pending_approval and decides nothing until an admin approves it. Which one you get depends on your role and on security.require_approval_for_agent_rules — not on the request.
⚠️ Role restrictions are per rule TYPE: an agent key cannot create certain types and a dev key cannot create signer_restriction, both 403.
⚠️ A rule created active immediately re-evaluates pending sign requests in the background, so creating one can approve something that was already waiting.

202.description: stored as pending_approval; inert until an admin approves

403.description: read-only mode, a rule type your role may not create, or the per-key rule limit

503.description: the rule type needs a toolchain (e.g. forge) that is not available

post.description:
Runs the stored test cases of every enabled evm_js rule. Changes nothing and takes no request body.
⛔ Admin ROLE only, 403 otherwise.
⚠️ Always 200: failures are in `results[].valid` and in `passed`/`failed`, never in the status code.
⚠️ `full=true` loads every rule into one engine so cross-rule interference shows up. It silently falls back to isolated mode when no JS evaluator is wired — the response does not say which mode ran.

parameters.description: only the literal `true` selects full-engine mode
parameters.name: full

403.description: admin role required

delete.description:
⚠️ Deletes the rule's budgets with it.
⛔ Refused with 403 for: read-only mode, a config-sourced rule, an immutable rule, someone else's rule, and a synthetic simulation rule unless you are admin and it was auto-generated.

403.description: Forbidden

get.description: ⚠️ An id that is not a well-formed rule id is 400, not 404.

patch.description:
Partial. ⛔ Like templates, `name` / `description` / `type` are plain strings, so an empty one means «leave unchanged» rather than «clear».
⛔ Four things are un-updatable and all answer 403: a config-sourced rule, an immutable rule, a synthetic `sim:` budget rule, and someone else's rule.
⚠️ Only admin may change `applied_to`.

403.description: read-only mode, config-sourced, immutable, synthetic, not yours, or a type/applied_to your role may not set

post.description:
Takes no request body. ⛔ Admin ROLE only, checked in the handler as 403 — the route's list_rules permission is not what gates this.
⚠️ A rule that is not in pending_approval is 400, and the message names its current status.
⚠️ Approving a PROPOSAL applies the proposed changes to the target rule. If the target has since been deleted the answer is 409 and the proposal is rejected; if the target became immutable it is 403.

parameters.description: rule id, or the id of a proposal
parameters.name: id

400.description: not pending approval, or the proposed change fails validation

403.description: admin role required, or the target rule is immutable

409.description: the target rule of this proposal no longer exists

get.description:
⚠️ Returns a bare JSON ARRAY, not an object with a `budgets` key — unlike the collection endpoint at /api/v1/evm/budgets.
⚠️ An unknown rule id is 200 with an empty array, not 404. Only an id longer than 128 characters is a 400.

post.description:
Zeroes spent and tx_count on every budget of this rule. Takes no request body.
⚠️ The 200 body has a single key `reset` — how many budget rows were zeroed, which is 0 when the rule had none.

For keys that may not edit a rule directly: creates a SEPARATE pending rule row pointing at the target. Always 202 — nothing changes on the target until an admin approves the proposal.
⛔ Only agent and admin roles may propose; everyone else is 403.
⚠️ An empty body is a 400 («at least one field must be changed»), but no individual field is required — which is why none is marked so.
⚠️ A second pending proposal from the same key for the same rule is 409.

parameters.name: id

post.description:
⛔ Admin ROLE only, 403 otherwise.
⚠️ The body is optional AND unvalidated: a malformed one is swallowed and the rule is still rejected, with an empty reason. Sending no body at all works the same way.
⚠️ A rule that is not in pending_approval is 400.

schema.description: optional reason; a malformed body is ignored, not rejected

requestBody.description: optional reason; a malformed body is ignored, not rejected

403.description: admin role required

post.description:
Changes nothing and takes no request body.
⛔ Admin ROLE only, 403 otherwise. ⛔ evm_js rules only — any other type is 400.
⚠️ A rule with no test cases is 200 with an empty result set, which reads as a pass.

400.description: not an evm_js rule, or its test_cases do not parse

403.description: admin role required

post.description:
The core endpoint. Runs the rule engine: blocklist, then whitelist, then budget, then manual approval.
⛔ A 200 does NOT mean a signature. When no rule matched and manual approval is enabled, the response is 200 with `status` set to a pending/authorizing state and `signature` absent — a client must branch on `status`, not on the HTTP code.
⚠️ 403 covers four different things, distinguishable only by the message: no access to the signer, the signer is awaiting admin approval, the signer is locked, and \"no matching rule and manual approval is disabled\".
⚠️ A signer whose key material is missing is 409, not 404 — the signer exists, its material does not.
⚠️ 404 and the locked-signer 403 deliberately tell a caller apart states that a stricter API would merge; that is an accepted risk recorded in the handler, not an oversight.

200.description: signed, OR accepted and awaiting approval — read `status`

400.description: missing or malformed field, oversized payload, or a payload the chain adapter rejected

403.description: no signer access, signer pending approval, signer locked, or no rule matched with manual approval off

409.description: the signer exists but its key material is unavailable

post.description:
Up to 20 transactions, all for the SAME chain_id and the SAME signer_address, all with sign_type \"transaction\". A mismatch anywhere is 400.
⛔ All-or-nothing: one transaction blocked by a rule fails the WHOLE batch with 403 and nothing is signed. There is no partial success in the 200 body.
⚠️ When no rule matches, the batch can still be approved by simulation. A simulation that detects an approval, or that cannot run, is 403 — not a 503 — so \"the simulator is down\" and \"your batch was refused\" arrive as the same status.
⚠️ `net_balance_changes` is present only when simulation actually ran.

400.description: empty or oversized batch, a malformed item, or items that disagree on chain_id / signer_address

403.description: no signer access, a rule blocked one transaction, or no rule matched and simulation did not auto-approve

get.description:
⛔ Scoped per caller: a non-admin is pinned to its own signers, and naming another key in `api_key_id` is 403 rather than an empty list. `ownership_status=pending_approval` is admin-only, also 403.
⚠️ `locked` and `enabled` are tri-state: absent means no filter, and anything that is not `true`/`false` is a 400.
⚠️ `exclude_hd_derived` only recognises `true` and `1`; any other value leaves derived addresses in.

post.description:
⛔ A signer created by a NON-ADMIN key lands in pending_approval and cannot sign until an admin calls the approve endpoint. The 201 does not tell you which happened — check the signer's ownership status.
⚠️ Three creation modes share one body, chosen inside `keystore`: both import fields empty generates a fresh keypair, `private_key_hex` imports a raw key, `keystore_json` imports a v3 keystore. Sending both import fields is 400.
⛔ Password, private key and keystore JSON are zeroised after handoff and never echoed back; the response carries only the address and labels.
⚠️ A failure to record ownership is logged but does NOT fail the 201 — the signer exists with no owner and has to be fixed by hand.

403.description: read-only mode, or the per-key keystore limit is reached

Dry-run against the configured simulation backend. Signs nothing, broadcasts nothing, and does not consult the rule engine.
⚠️ A reverting transaction is a SUCCESSFUL simulation: 200 with `success:false` and the revert fields filled in. 500 means the simulator itself could not run, not that the transaction failed.

⚠️ Any repository error answers 404, including a real failure — the handler does not distinguish them.

Creates one rule instance per template_id, in a single transaction.
⛔ Test cases ALWAYS run: `skip_validation: true` is a 400 and a missing JS evaluator is a 503. There is no bypass, on purpose (validation_mandatory.go).
⚠️ Almost every failure after the preset loads is a 400, including validation failures and commit failures — the status does not tell a client whether to retry.

patch.description:
Partial. ⛔ But not in the usual way: `name` and `description` are plain strings, so an EMPTY string means \"leave unchanged\" and there is no way to clear either through this endpoint. Only `enabled` is a pointer and can be set to false.
⛔ A template that came from config.yaml cannot be updated through the API at all: 403.

403.description: read-only mode, or the template came from config.yaml

post.description:
⛔ Test cases ALWAYS run: `skip_validation: true` is a 400 and a missing JS evaluator is a 503. There is no bypass (validation_mandatory.go).
⚠️ The 201 body is an untyped object, not a named schema: it always carries `rule`, and carries `budget`, `sub_rules` and `sub_budgets` only when the template produced them (a template_bundle expands into sub-rules). A marshal failure on the optional parts is logged and the key is simply omitted from an otherwise successful 201.
⚠️ Whether the new instance is active or waits for approval is decided by the caller's role and the security settings, not by this request.

400.description: bad body, bad expires_in or schedule period, unresolvable template, skip_validation, or failed test cases

get.description:
Unauthenticated on purpose: orchestrators scrape it and `remote-signer server status` calls it before any API key exists.
⚠️ It answers with more than liveness — version plus a security summary. `security` is absent entirely until SetSecurityConfig has been called, and `security.approval_guard` is absent when the guard is disabled.
